title: Perimeter, Area and Volume of Rectangles and Rectangular Prisms
seo_title: Grade 6 Perimeter, Area and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Measure perimeter using rulers or measuring tapes; measurement of area: find areas of regular and irregular shapes by counting squares on grids, and investigate the relationship between the area and the lengths of rectangles; measurement of volume: find the volume of rectangular prisms by packing or counting cubes, and investigate the relationship between volume and the length, breadth and height.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 perimeter, area and volume worksheets: perimeter, area of rectangles and composite shapes and volume of rectangular prisms. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Area = l × b. Volume = l × b × h.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter: add all the sides. Rectangle: 2 × (length + breadth).
  • Area of a rectangle: length × breadth, in square units (cm², m²).
  • For a composite shape, split it into rectangles.
  • Volume of a rectangular prism: length × breadth × height, in cubic units (cm³).

Examples

Example

A box 6 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm

6 × 4 = 24 cubes in a layer

5 layers

Answer: 120 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Two sides onlyAdd all four sides.
Area or perimeter?Area is inside; perimeter is around.
Adding for volumeMultiply length, breadth and height.

faq.a: Measure perimeter, find areas of regular and irregular shapes, and find the volume of rectangular prisms, using square and cubic units.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 14 + 2 × 9 = 28 + 18 = 46 cm. 14 + 9 = 23 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 23 + 2 × 17 = 46 + 34 = 80 m. 23 + 17 = 40 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 8,5 + 2 × 4 = 17 + 8 = 25 cm. 8,5 + 4 = 12,5 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 12,5 + 2 × 7,5 = 25 + 15 = 40 m. 12,5 + 7,5 = 20 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 6,4 + 2 × 3,8 = 12,8 + 7,6 = 20,4 cm. 6,4 + 3,8 = 10,2 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 145 + 2 × 90 = 290 + 180 = 470 m. 145 + 90 = 235 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 2,75 + 2 × 1,5 = 5,5 + 3 = 8,5 m. 2,75 + 1,5 = 4,25 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 36 + 2 × 24 = 72 + 48 = 120 m. 36 + 24 = 60 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: This is a square. What is its perimeter?
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal: 4 × 13,5 = 54 cm. 2 × 13,5 = 27 counts only two sides.

items.q: This is a square. What is its perimeter?
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal: 4 × 48 = 192 m. 2 × 48 = 96 counts only two sides.

items.q: All the sides of this equilateral triangle are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. Multiply: 3 × 12,5 = 37,5 cm. 12,5 × 4 = 50 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular pentagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides. Multiply: 5 × 14 = 70 cm. 14 × 4 = 56 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this equilateral triangle are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. Multiply: 3 × 45 = 135 mm. 45 × 4 = 180 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular hexagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Multiply: 6 × 9,5 = 57 cm. 9,5 × 4 = 38 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular octagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. Multiply: 8 × 15 = 120 cm. 15 × 4 = 60 would treat it like a square.

items.q: A regular octagon has a perimeter of 96 cm. Which number sentence finds the length of one side?
items.e: An octagon has 8 equal sides, so share the perimeter into 8 parts: 96 ÷ 8 = 12 cm.

items.q: All the sides of this regular decagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular decagon has 10 equal sides. Multiply: 10 × 6 = 60 m. 6 × 4 = 24 would treat it like a square.

items.q: A regular hexagon has a perimeter of 57 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides: 57 ÷ 6 = 9,5 cm. Check: 6 × 9,5 = 57. Dividing by 4 only works for a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular hexagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Multiply: 6 × 2,5 = 15 m. 2,5 × 4 = 10 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular decagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular decagon has 10 equal sides. Multiply: 10 × 12,5 = 125 cm. 12,5 × 4 = 50 would treat it like a square.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 3 rows of 5 squares: 3 × 5 = 15 cm². (16 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 2 rows of 7 squares: 2 × 7 = 14 cm². (18 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 4 rows of 6 squares: 4 × 6 = 24 cm². (20 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 3 rows of 8 squares: 3 × 8 = 24 cm². (22 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: 4 rows of 9 squares: 4 × 9 = 36 cm². (26 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded square?
items.e: 5 rows of 5 squares: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². (20 cm would be the distance around it, the perimeter.)

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of 1 cm² squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: There are 7 squares in each row and 3 rows. 3 × 7 = 21 squares, so the area is 21 cm². This is why area = length × width.

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of 1 cm² squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: There are 6 squares in each row and 5 rows. 5 × 6 = 30 squares, so the area is 30 cm². This is why area = length × width.

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of 1 cm² squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: There are 9 squares in each row and 4 rows. 4 × 9 = 36 squares, so the area is 36 cm². This is why area = length × width.

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². (26 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (30 cm), not the area.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 14 × 5 = 70 m². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (38 m), not the area.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 cm². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (40 cm), not the area.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 15 × 7 = 105 m². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (44 m), not the area.

items.q: The dashed line splits the shape into two rectangles. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 8 × 3 = 24. Add: 42 + 24 = 66 cm². Use each part once: 6 × 7 + 14 × 3 = 84 counts the 6 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: The dashed line splits the shape into two rectangles. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 49 + 15 = 64 m². Use each part once: 7 × 7 + 12 × 3 = 85 counts the 7 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape?
items.e: Whole rectangle 15 × 11 = 165, take away the missing corner 9 × 5 = 45: 165 − 45 = 120 cm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 6 × 11 = 66 and 9 × 6 = 54. Add: 66 + 54 = 120 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape?
items.e: Whole rectangle 11 × 7 = 77, take away the missing corner 5 × 3 = 15: 77 − 15 = 62 m². Or: split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 5 × 4 = 20. Add: 42 + 20 = 62 m².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape? Find the two missing lengths first.
items.e: Missing lengths: 14 − 8 = 6 and 10 − 4 = 6. Whole rectangle 14 × 10 = 140, take away the missing corner 6 × 6 = 36: 140 − 36 = 104 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape? Find the two missing lengths first.
items.e: Missing lengths: 13 − 7 = 6 and 11 − 5 = 6. Whole rectangle 13 × 11 = 143, take away the missing corner 6 × 6 = 36: 143 − 36 = 107 m².

items.q: All 12 sides of this plus shape are 2,5 cm long. What is its perimeter?
items.e: 12 sides × 2,5 cm = 30 cm. 10 cm uses only 4 sides. Count the sides carefully: 3 on each arm, 4 arms.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this shape?
items.e: Add all 8 sides: 4,5 + 7,5 + 9 + 7,5 + 4,5 + 12 + 18 + 12 = 75 m. The notch adds two 7,5 m sides, so the answer is more than the 60 m of a plain 18 m by 12 m rectangle.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. Each notch in this H shape is 6 m wide and 4 m deep. What is the perimeter?
items.e: Count the sides first: 12. Each notch has two 4 m sides and one 6 m side. Add them all: 3 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 11 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 11 = 62 m. 46 m is the rectangle around it, which leaves out the four 4 m sides that go in and out of the notches.

items.q: A corner was cut off a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
items.e: Add the 5 sides, including the slanted one: 9 + 5 + 4 + 12 + 8 = 38 cm. 40 cm is the perimeter of the whole rectangle before the corner was cut.

items.q: A corner was cut off a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
items.e: Add the 5 sides, including the slanted one: 16 + 9 + 12 + 5 + 6 = 48 m. 50 m is the perimeter of the whole rectangle before the corner was cut.

items.q: A rectangle and a triangle are put together. What is the perimeter of the whole shape?
items.e: Go around the outside only: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 + 8 = 34 cm. The dashed line is inside the shape, so it is not part of the perimeter. Adding the two perimeters (26 + 24 = 50) counts the inside line twice.

items.q: A rectangle and a triangle are put together. What is the perimeter of the whole shape?
items.e: Go around the outside only: 6,5 + 4,5 + 9 + 4,5 + 6,5 = 31 m. The dashed line is inside the shape, so it is not part of the perimeter. Adding the two perimeters (27 + 22 = 49) counts the inside line twice.

items.q: Two rectangles, each 8 cm by 3 cm, are put end to end so their 3 cm sides touch. They make one long rectangle. What is its perimeter?
items.e: The new rectangle is 8 + 8 = 16 cm long and 3 cm wide: 2 × (16 + 3) = 38 cm. 44 cm adds the two perimeters (22 + 22) and counts the two 3 cm sides that are now inside.

items.q: Five squares with 4 cm sides are put in a row, side by side. What is the perimeter of the row?
items.e: The row is 5 × 4 = 20 cm long and 4 cm tall: 2 × (20 + 4) = 48 cm. 80 cm (5 × 16) counts the sides where the squares touch, which are inside.

items.q: Ethan puts two equilateral triangles with 6 cm sides together along one side. They make a 4-sided shape. What is its perimeter?
items.e: The new shape has 4 outside sides of 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. 36 cm adds both triangles (18 + 18) and counts the shared side twice.

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 5 = 40 and 19 × 7 = 133. Add them: 40 + 133 = 173 cm². (Or 19 × 12 − 11 × 5 = 173 cm².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 7 = 56 and 19 × 5 = 95. Add them: 56 + 95 = 151 m². (Or 19 × 12 − 11 × 7 = 151 m².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 4 = 32 and 19 × 6 = 114. Add them: 32 + 114 = 146 cm². (Or 19 × 10 − 11 × 4 = 146 cm².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 5 = 40 and 18 × 4 = 72. Add them: 40 + 72 = 112 m². (Or 18 × 9 − 10 × 5 = 112 m².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 5 = 30 and 14 × 4 = 56. Add them: 30 + 56 = 86 cm². (Or 14 × 9 − 8 × 5 = 86 cm².)

items.q: What is the area of this shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 13 × 4 = 52 and 20 × 6 = 120. Add them: 52 + 120 = 172 m². (Or 20 × 10 − 7 × 4 = 172 m².)

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 17 − 6 = 11 m and 9 − 5 = 4 m. Split into two rectangles: 11 × 5 = 55 and 17 × 4 = 68. Area = 55 + 68 = 123 m².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 13 − 7 = 6 cm and 9 − 5 = 4 cm. Split into two rectangles: 6 × 5 = 30 and 13 × 4 = 52. Area = 30 + 52 = 82 cm².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 18 − 10 = 8 m and 14 − 5 = 9 m. Split into two rectangles: 8 × 5 = 40 and 18 × 9 = 162. Area = 40 + 162 = 202 m².

items.q: Two sides are not labelled. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 14 − 8 = 6 cm and 7 − 4 = 3 cm. Split into two rectangles: 6 × 4 = 24 and 14 × 3 = 42. Area = 24 + 42 = 66 cm².

items.q: A cube has edges that are 1 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: A cube with 1 cm edges is the unit for volume: 1 cm³ (one cubic centimetre). 1 cm² is the area of one face, and 1 cm is the length of one edge.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 3 layers: 9 × 3 = 27 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 19 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 2 rows of 4 cubes = 8 cubes. There are 4 layers: 8 × 4 = 32 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 23 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 4 layers: 4 × 4 = 16 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 13 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 2 layers: 4 × 2 = 8 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 7 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 4 layers: 10 × 4 = 40 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 28 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes = 15 cubes. There are 3 layers: 15 × 3 = 45 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 29 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 3 layers: 10 × 3 = 30 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too: only 22 cubes show a face.

items.q: How many centimetre cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes long and 4 cubes deep: 5 × 4 = 20 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 2 = 10 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: How many centimetre cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 4 cubes long and 3 cubes deep: 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. The front face shows 4 × 4 = 16 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 3 × 7 = 33 × 7 = 231 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 4 × 2 = 44 × 2 = 88 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 9 × 3 × 9 = 27 × 9 = 243 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 2 × 4 = 12 × 4 = 48 m³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 13 × 3 × 11 = 39 × 11 = 429 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 7 × 5 = 77 × 5 = 385 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 4 = 12 × 4 = 48 m³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 14 × 5 × 11 = 70 × 11 = 770 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 5 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal, so V = 5 × 5 × 5 = 25 × 5 = 125 cm³. 5 × 3 = 15 is not the volume.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 8 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal, so V = 8 × 8 × 8 = 64 × 8 = 512 cm³. 8 × 3 = 24 is not the volume.

items.q: A bathroom floor is 3 m long and 2 m wide. It is tiled with square tiles 50 cm by 50 cm. How many tiles are needed?
items.e: Along the length: 300 cm ÷ 50 cm = 6 tiles. Across: 200 cm ÷ 50 cm = 4 tiles. 6 × 4 = 24 tiles. (6 is the area in m², not the number of tiles.)

items.q: A bathroom wall is 2,4 m wide and 2 m high. It is covered with square tiles 20 cm by 20 cm. How many tiles are needed?
items.e: Across: 240 ÷ 20 = 12 tiles. Up: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 tiles. 12 × 10 = 120 tiles.

items.q: A backyard is 9 m by 5 m. A concrete patio 3 m by 2 m is in one corner. The rest gets turf. How many square metres of turf are needed?
items.e: Backyard: 9 × 5 = 45 m². Patio: 3 × 2 = 6 m². Turf: 45 − 6 = 39 m². (40 comes from taking away 3 + 2.)

items.q: A wall is 6 m long and 2,5 m high. It needs two coats of paint. One litre of paint covers 10 m². How many litres are needed?
items.e: Wall: 6 × 2,5 = 15 m². Two coats: 2 × 15 = 30 m². 30 ÷ 10 = 3 ℓ. (1,5 ℓ is only one coat.)

items.q: A bedroom wall is 4 m long and 3 m high. It has a window 1,5 m by 1 m. What area of wall needs painting?
items.e: Wall: 4 × 3 = 12 m². Window: 1,5 × 1 = 1,5 m². 12 − 1,5 = 10,5 m². (9,5 comes from taking away 1,5 + 1.)

items.q: A patio is 5 m long and 4,5 m wide. Each box of pavers covers 2 m². How many boxes are needed?
items.e: Area: 5 × 4,5 = 22,5 m². 22,5 ÷ 2 = 11,25, so 11 boxes are not enough. Buy 12 boxes.

items.q: A backyard pool is 10 m long and 4 m wide. The pool cover must be 0,5 m bigger than the pool on every side. What is the area of the cover?
items.e: 0,5 m on each side adds 1 m to each measurement: 11 m by 5 m. Area: 11 × 5 = 55 m². (47,25 comes from adding 0,5 m only once: 10,5 × 4,5.)

items.q: Amahle’s class has a vegetable garden bed 4 m long and 2,5 m wide. Each seedling needs 0,5 m². How many seedlings fit in the bed?
items.e: Area: 4 × 2,5 = 10 m². 10 ÷ 0,5 = 20 seedlings (there are 2 halves in each square metre).

items.q: A solar panel is 1,7 m long and 1 m wide. A school puts 12 panels on the roof of the hall. What area do the panels cover?
Busisiwe’s bedroom is 4,5 m by 4 m. Mpho’s bedroom is 6 m by 3 m. Which bedroom has the larger floor area?
items.e: Busisiwe: 4,5 × 4 = 18 m². Mpho: 6 × 3 = 18 m². The areas are the same, even though the perimeters (17 m and 18 m) are different.

items.q: A juice box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 10 cm high. How much juice can it hold?
items.e: V = 6 × 4 × 10 = 240 cm³. 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ, so it holds 240 mℓ. (2,4 ℓ would be 2 400 mℓ.)

items.q: A shoebox is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 12 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 30 × 20 × 12 = 600 × 12 = 7 200 cm³. 600 is only the base, and volume is in cm³, not cm².

items.q: Liam’s fish tank is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres does it hold when full?
Liam fills the same fish tank (60 cm long, 30 cm wide, 40 cm high) only up to 35 cm. How much water is in it?
items.e: Use the height of the water, not the tank: 60 × 30 × 35 = 1 800 × 35 = 63 000 cm³ = 63 ℓ. 9 ℓ is the empty space at the top.

items.q: Lungile’s fish tank is 50 cm long, 25 cm wide and 30 cm high. How many litres does it hold when full?
A cooler for a class field trip is 40 cm long, 30 cm wide and 25 cm deep inside. How many litres does it hold?
Sibusiso’s lunch container is 15 cm long, 10 cm wide and 6 cm high. Will 1 ℓ of soup fit in it?
items.e: V = 15 × 10 × 6 = 900 cm³ = 900 mℓ. 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ, so no: 100 mℓ of soup would not fit.

items.q: Box A is 8 cm × 5 cm × 4 cm. Box B is 6 cm × 6 cm × 5 cm. Which box has the greater volume, and by how much?
items.e: A: 8 × 5 × 4 = 160 cm³. B: 6 × 6 × 5 = 180 cm³. 180 − 160 = 20, so B is greater by 20 cm³. Adding the edges gives 17 for both boxes, which is why “the same” is a trap.

items.q: A tissue box is a cube with edges 12 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 12 × 12 × 12 = 144 × 12 = 1 728 cm³. 144 is only one face, and 36 adds the edges.

items.q: How many 2 cm cubes fit in a box that is 10 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high?
items.e: Along the length: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cubes. Across: 6 ÷ 2 = 3. Up: 4 ÷ 2 = 2. 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubes. 240 counts 1 cm cubes, and 120 divides by 2 only once.
